units: USD millions; margins and expense ratios are decimal fractions
status: AI-assisted working analyst assumptions; no company long-term guidance or final valuation claimed

Q26.locators: Note 18 segment gross profit; MD&A costs, R&D and SG&A; Note 13 cancellation

RELEASE26.locators: Q3 GAAP guidance; Q2 income statement

conventions.2026: H1 actual reported expenses plus Q3/Q4 estimates; show the H1 cancellation separately in a normalized operating view. Do not remove it twice or alter historical cash.
conventions.gross_profit: 2026 uses consolidated quarterly GAAP-basis margin assumptions. From 2027, continuing launch and space margins include their allocated production overhead, D&A and compensation. Incremental Neutron contribution less separate fixed commercial readiness costs forms its gross profit.
conventions.neutron_cost_scope: Fixed commercial readiness costs are an assumed manufacturing/launch-operations overhead pool, distinct from technical development in total-company R&D and from continuing-launch costs. This allocation is not disclosed by management. Avoid adding another copy during statement integration; test overlap sensitivity.
conventions.rd: Total-company R&D, net, expensed in dollars; no invented separately reported Neutron budget or capitalization. Includes regular compensation and D&A.
conventions.sga: 2027 onward: explicit fixed overhead plus a revenue-linked allowance. Includes ordinary compensation, D&A and a retained allowance for transaction/administrative costs; no blanket non-GAAP addback.
conventions.cash_flow: Operating profit is before interest and taxes. D&A and ordinary SBC are included in expenses here. Their noncash/cash-replacement treatment must be reconciled once in the linked statements; no additional D&A expense subtraction.
conventions.transaction_scope: Same standalone owned-business scope as revenue; no Iridium revenue, synergies or combined-company cost forecast.

downside.story: Missed deliveries lower utilization and margin, while technical delays sustain R&D and readiness costs. Q3 deliberately misses both margin and expense guidance.

base.story: Q3 follows guidance midpoints, followed by modest Q4 margin recovery. Continuing-business efficiency improves gradually; Neutron initially loses money after commercial overhead; R&D and total SG&A rise in dollars.

upside.story: Higher utilization and favorable mix support margins. More launches and products require higher dollar R&D, commercial overhead and SG&A; investment and funding still need separate modeling.

driver_challenges.basis: Base Q3 30% is management's 29-31% GAAP midpoint; Q4 32% is an analyst recovery assumption. Downside 26/27%; upside 31/35%.
driver_challenges.challenge: Product mix, execution losses and purchase accounting can depress margins. H1 margin does not guarantee the next quarter.
driver_challenges.change_evidence: Dated contract-cost estimates, delivery mix and updated GAAP guidance.

driver_challenges.basis: Base Q3 85+61=146 matches the 143-149 GAAP operating-expense midpoint, with split informed by Q2 82.429 R&D and 59.661 SG&A. Q4 88+64=152 is an analyst estimate. Other splits are scenario judgments.
driver_challenges.challenge: Management did not guide the R&D/SG&A split; integration and development costs can overshoot.
driver_challenges.change_evidence: Staffing, engineering milestones, transaction-expense breakdown and updated expense guidance.

driver_challenges.basis: Base 43/44/45/45% is near H1 launch gross margin and assumes modest efficiency gains; downside 35-38% and upside 45-50% test utilization and mix.
driver_challenges.challenge: HASTE recognition and mission mix can distort period margins; 50% is an optimistic analyst endpoint, not a validated unit-cost target.
driver_challenges.change_evidence: Sustained like-for-like launch costs, mission mix and facility utilization.

driver_challenges.basis: Base 34-37% surrounds and gradually improves on H1 segment gross margin. Downside 27-30%; upside 36-42% reflect integration, mix and execution.
driver_challenges.challenge: Fixed-price contract revisions or acquired-business costs can outweigh scale economies.
driver_challenges.change_evidence: Program cost-to-complete updates, repeatable component margins and acquisition integration results.

driver_challenges.driver: Neutron contribution margin and fixed commercial costs
driver_challenges.basis: Analyst split: base contribution 20/25/30/35% less 25/30/35/40 million fixed costs. Models negative initial gross profit and costs without revenue. No company program-cost disclosure supports these precise amounts.
driver_challenges.challenge: Weakly evidenced allocation; costs may overlap existing production costs or R&D, and technical performance/reuse can miss expectations.
driver_challenges.change_evidence: Separate commercial-production cost schedule, achieved cadence and reuse economics. Test fixed-cost removal for overlap and cost escalation for execution risk.

driver_challenges.basis: Base 350/360/375/390 million grows from the new 2026 estimate, instead of carrying Lab 10's 290-330 path unchanged. Downside retains 385-440 despite weak sales; upside funds expansion at 370-445.
driver_challenges.challenge: Milestone delays can extend spending; spending less could also reduce future products. No causal return-on-R&D is proven.
driver_challenges.change_evidence: Engineering staffing, qualified hardware, product readiness and disclosed grant funding. Model revenue consequences alongside discretionary cuts.

driver_challenges.driver: SG&A fixed overhead and revenue-linked allowance
driver_challenges.basis: Base fixed 150 million grows 5% yearly plus 8% of revenue. This roughly continues 2026 dollar expense and allows operating leverage. Downside uses 9%; upside 7.5%, with different fixed growth paths.
driver_challenges.challenge: This is a modeling decomposition, not a disclosed fixed/variable split. Legal, insurance, integration and compliance expenses may be sticky or rise faster.
driver_challenges.change_evidence: Headcount, overhead budgets, transaction-cost detail and demonstrated expense scaling; avoid assuming proportional cost cuts in a revenue miss.
